 Advertisement Heavy rain boosts Oklahoma lake levels but drought concerns remain
 Recent rainfall in Oklahoma has improved lake levels and farm ponds, but the state remains in a significant drought and needs more rain for full recovery.
 Advertisement Updated: 4:38 PM CDT Oct 19, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Michael Armstrong Meteorologist Heavy rain boosts Oklahoma lake levels but drought concerns remain
 Recent rainfall in Oklahoma has improved lake levels and farm ponds, but the state remains in a significant drought and needs more rain for full recovery.
 Updated: 4:38 PM CDT Oct 19, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Michael Armstrong Meteorologist Nearly a foot of rain in parts of Oklahoma last week brought much-needed relief, filling farm ponds and raising water levels in lakes across central and western parts of the state.
 KOCO 5 Field Meteorologist Michael Armstrong said the rain's impact was incredible. Just a couple of weeks ago, Michael walked out to the middle of a pond here in Edmond. Now, he would need a boat or a swimsuit.
 Advertisement Just weeks ago, the same pond was nearly dry after months of little to no rain. Lake Hefner, which had dropped nearly eight feet below normal since July, also saw significant improvement. 
 The lake had experienced exposed shorelines and limited access for boating and fishing, but the recent rainfall, combined with a water release from Canton Lake , has helped its recovery. 
 >> Video Below: Recent rain boosts Lake Hefner levels, but Lake Canton remains low 
 Despite the improvement, Lake Hefner remains five feet below normal. 
 Meteorologists will get another update on the drought later this week, but it's safe to say that Oklahomans aren't out of it yet, and that helps highlight just how significant the ongoing drought is. 
 Significant additional rainfall is still needed across much of the state to help reservoirs, aquifers and agricultural lands fully recover. 
 On one hand, Oklahomans can be thankful for the rain that did come, but on the other hand, the state is going to need several more inches of rain to recover.
